_comment: Single source of truth for the Sprinter render core's 16-entry mode #82 palette (port.md section 3.5). tools/gen_sprinter_palette.py turns this into asm/sprinter/generated/palette_base.inc (the resident's boot palette, replacing asm/sprinter/video_s1.asm's old ad-hoc EGA ramp) and a runtime theme-table blob packed into the assets page. Index 15's RGB is a normal usable colour like any other: the hardware transparency key is a per-tile encoding (packed 4bpp nibble value 15 in tiles drawn through the keyed VRAM alias), independent of what this palette register displays -- see the note in port.md section 3.5 amended when S4 closed.

base.name: accent
base.desc: Accent -- sampled from the real Sprinter logo's brand blue.

base.name: cursor
base.desc: Input-line cursor / active-field highlight. Not a transparency reservation -- see the format note above.

_piece_comment: piece_allowed_indices: every palette entry an opaque pixel of a piece PNG may use. Pieces are NOT limited to a four-colour ramp -- a piece tile is ordinary opaque 4bpp data in this same 16-entry palette, so the HUD colours are available to piece art too. The four entries left out are the ones the packer paints UNDER the piece (2/3 board square, 8 move flash), where a piece pixel of that colour would be invisible, and 15, whose adjacent pairs pack to the 0xFF hardware key byte. tools/build_sprinter_piece_tiles.py derives the same list and tests/tools/test_sprinter_piece_tiles.py fails if the two drift apart. piece_import_quantize_indices: the smaller set tools/rasterize_sprinter_pieces.py quantizes a freshly imported SVG down to -- a starting point for hand editing, not a limit on the finished art.
_theme_comment: The five board themes the resident ships, mirroring asm/sprinter/video.asm's theme_squares_rgb table verbatim -- tests/tools/test_sprinter_palette.py parses that table back out of the .asm and fails if the two drift. The table is still hand-written on the Z80 side; generating it from here is part of the piece-set palette work (port.md section 3.5).
_piece_sets_comment: One palette per piece set: the four entries 4-7 are re-written when the player picks a set, exactly as a theme re-writes 2/3 (port.md section 3.5). Names and order must match assets/lichess/selected_next_sets.json's "selected" list -- tools/build_sprinter_piece_tiles.py validates each set's PNGs against ITS OWN four colours. Set 0 must equal the base palette (it is what boots). The four colours of a set must not collide with each other or with any other colour that can be on screen at the same time (0, 1, 8-15 and every theme's square colours): the packers invert the palette into an {rgb: index} map, so a shared value makes an index unreachable -- and on screen it would mean a piece the colour of the board or of a marker.
